decision: treated the OBS shutdown crash as part of the stability failure
why: four crashes share the same plugin teardown frame
result: confirmed openstream_unregister_dock releases an OBS source during shutdown

decision: tested the installed plugin with a current-format simulated phone
why: separates Linux plugin discovery from the unknown installed Android build

decision: tested a busy simulated phone reserved for the saved CAM A source
why: matches the phone's reported paired state instead of testing only a free phone
result: plugin discovered the busy phone and sent POST /reserve

decision: created a separate shin wire identity and removed the OBS dock
why: avoids source/plugin/app collisions and the proven dock teardown crash
result: shin uses dev.shin.app, shin_phone_source, SHIN/1, ports 51615/9100/9101, and no frontend or Widgets dependency

decision: added selected-host unicast to broadcast and multicast discovery
why: phones that receive OBS beacons must be able to advertise back even when reverse multicast is filtered
result: bounded one-second beacon loop now targets broadcast, multicast, and the selected OBS address

decision: built matched Android and Linux artifacts
why: both sides must share the same protocol before installation
result: Android succeeded; all 5 C++ tests passed

decision: installed shin and disabled the crashing OpenStream module recoverably
why: prevents both modules from loading and preserves rollback
result: shin-obs.so is the only third-party camera module loaded; scene backup created

decision: ran real OBS against a synthetic H.264/AAC SRT phone
why: verifies discovery, reservation, control, transport, decode, timestamps, frame output, release, and shutdown
result: OBS received 640x360 H.264 plus AAC, emitted decoded frames, released reservation, and exited with no new core dump

decision: fixed stale Linux CI artifact and dependency expectations
why: the renamed module and removed UI dependencies changed the packaging contract
result: Linux CI now verifies shin paths and rejects frontend, Widgets, or Network linkage; Windows keeps its existing artifact contract
